content.text:
The drawing shows a five-membered imidazolidine ring with these atoms in order:

- N1 is the lower nitrogen, bonded to the CH2 of the side chain.
- C2 carries a methyl group.
- N3 is the NH.
- C4 carries the NO2 group.
- C5 carries the Br and closes the ring back to N1.

The side chain is N1–CH2–C(=O)–C6H4–Cl, a 4-chlorophenyl ketone. All ring bonds are plain, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES written from N1: N1(CC(=O)c2ccc(Cl)cc2)C(C)NC([N+](=O)[O-])C1Br

Checking the ring closure: N1, then C(C) for C2 with its methyl, then N for N3, then C([N+](=O)[O-]) for C4, then C1Br for C5 closing to N1. This matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CC1NC([N+](=O)[O-])C(Br)N1CC(=O)c1ccc(Cl)cc1
